Who is bound: Retailers: s 2 defines 'retailer means a person who is the holder of a retailer authorisation'; s 88(1) prohibits selling energy unless the seller holds a retailer authorisation or is an exempt seller. Consent and hardship duties run to 'small customers' and 'residential customers'. s 53(2)-(3): any person carrying out energy marketing activities must comply with the Energy Marketing Rules, and an associate's failure is taken to be the retailer's failure. Applies in SA under s 4 of the SA Act (by proclamation); application in other participating jurisdictions is by their own application Acts (not checked). Clause text is paraphrased from the source. summary: National Energy Retail Law (Schedule to the National Energy Retail Law (South Australia) Act 2011). Bound: Retailers: s 2 defines 'retailer means a person who is the holder of a retailer authorisation'; s 88(1) prohibits selling energy unless the seller holds a retailer authorisation or is an exempt seller. Consent and hardship duties run to 'small customers' and 'residential customers'. s 53(2)-(3): any person carrying out energy marketing activities must comply with the Energy Marketing Rules, and an associate's failure is taken to be the retailer's failure. Applies in SA under s 4 of the SA Act (by proclamation); application in other participating jurisdictions is by their own application Acts (not checked).

clauses.heading: Requirement for explicit informed consent for certain transactions
clauses.text: A retailer must obtain a small customer's explicit informed consent before transferring the customer from another retailer or entering the customer into a market retail contract, among other listed transactions.
clauses.notes: Provision read: 38. An agent that treats silence, a vague 'sounds good' or a question as agreement and switches or signs the customer up breaches the consent requirement. Note 2 states s 38 is a civil penalty provision.

clauses.heading: Nature of explicit informed consent
clauses.text: Consent is explicit informed consent only if the retailer, or a person acting for it, clearly, fully and adequately disclosed all matters relevant to the consent, including each specific purpose or use.
clauses.notes: Provision read: 39. An agent acting on behalf of the retailer that obtains consent without disclosing the relevant terms (price, term, fees, conditional discounts) or without verifiable verbal or written consent under s 39(2) produces no valid consent.

clauses.heading: No or defective explicit informed consent
clauses.text: A transfer or contract requiring explicit informed consent is void if it is established that the consent was not obtained.
clauses.notes: Provision read: 41. An agent that tells a customer disputing an unwanted switch that they are locked in, or that nothing can be done, misstates the customer's rights (raise within 12 months; retailer must produce the record within 10 business days).

clauses.heading: Obligation of retailer to communicate customer hardship policy
clauses.text: A retailer must tell a residential customer about its customer hardship policy where it appears that non-payment of an energy bill is due to hardship.
clauses.notes: Provision read: 46. An agent that hears signs of hardship (job loss, illness, cannot pay) and only demands payment, without telling the customer about the hardship policy, causes the retailer to breach s 46.

clauses.heading: General principle regarding de-energisation (or disconnection) of premises of hardship customers
clauses.text: A retailer must give effect to the principle that disconnecting a hardship customer's premises for inability to pay should be a last resort.
clauses.notes: Provision read: 47. An agent that threatens immediate disconnection to a hardship customer, or presents disconnection as the first or only option, contradicts the last resort principle.

clauses.heading: Payment plans
clauses.text: A retailer must offer and apply payment plans for hardship customers and for other residential customers who tell it, in writing or by phone, that they are experiencing payment difficulties.
clauses.notes: Provision read: 50(1). An agent that refuses, fails to offer, or discourages a payment plan after a residential customer says they cannot pay breaches s 50(1), which is a civil penalty provision. Exceptions exist only in circumstances specified in the Rules (s 50(2)).

clauses.heading: Debt recovery
clauses.text: A retailer must not start proceedings to recover an energy debt from a residential customer who is keeping to a payment plan or agreed arrangement, or where the retailer has not complied with its hardship policy or the Law and Rules for that customer.
clauses.notes: Provision read: 51. An agent that threatens legal action or debt collection against a customer who is keeping to a payment plan misstates the retailer's lawful options.

clauses.heading: Energy Marketing Rules
clauses.text: A person carrying out energy marketing activities must comply with the Energy Marketing Rules.
clauses.notes: Provision read: 53(2). An AI sales or retention agent is carrying out energy marketing activities; non-compliance with the NERR Energy Marketing Rules is a civil penalty breach and is attributed to the retailer under s 53(3).
